data.topic: AI agent self-learning and behavioral conditioning — refactoring our memory pipeline to close the feedback loop
data.input_summary: Refactor the existing memory/self-learning pipeline to close three broken feedback channels: (1) create the missing decision_preferences table so Stage 2 signal processing can correlate corrections to decisions, (2) create the missing compliance/ directory so Stage 5 hook generation can produce enforcement hooks, (3) render decision scores into session context so negatively-scored decisions influence future behavior.

constraints.value: Python/Bash/SQL orchestration infrastructure for Claude Code CLI. SQLite (epics.db, run-state.db, openmemory.sqlite), Ollama for embeddings (nomic-embed-text), shell hooks for session lifecycle.
No training-time RLHF, no fine-tuning, no weight updates. All behavioral conditioning must happen at inference time via prompt injection, structural guardrails, or statistical scoring.
Existing working components (correction detection, threshold promotion, rendered-prefs, OpenMemory storage, trust calibration) must not be disrupted.

Write targets limited to: load-session-context.sh (schema migration + decision score rendering), stop_processor.py (Stage 5 mkdir fix), and potentially signal_processor.py (if decision_preferences integration needs adjustment). Hook_generator.py code is already correct — just needs its output directory.
